title: Case: Recipient reports a wrong house number on a kettle parcel due out tomorrow
context: A kettle parcel is booked for delivery tomorrow. Routing control at the carrier owns address corrections and checks them against the merchant order record; the desk cannot change a label.
initial_request: Copy of what I put on the portal just now: Order TG-933, the house number on the label is wrong, it says 8 Dunmere Close and it should be 18. same postcode. its going out for delivery tmrw so pls get it changed before then. Emailing this as well in case the portal doesnt go through, its been playing up all week

events.body: Order TG-933, the house number on the label is wrong, it says 8 Dunmere Close and it should be 18. same postcode. its going out for delivery tmrw so pls get it changed before then. Emailing this as well in case the portal doesnt go through, its been playing up all week

Address correction request for DL-933 (order TG-933), booked for delivery 2026-04-15. The recipient, Bram Tolliver, says the label reads 8 Dunmere Close and should read 18 Dunmere Close, same postcode. Please check against the order record, confirm whether the label can be corrected before route load, and confirm the outcome to him.

Your portal message came through. I have passed the house-number correction for DL-933 to Routing control at Plover Arc, who own address changes. I can't make or confirm the change myself; they will tell you whether it has been made.

events.to: Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk; Bram Tolliver, recipient
events.body: Received. Logged as ADR-933 for DL-933 (8 to 18 Dunmere Close, postcode unchanged). We check it against the merchant order record and will confirm either way to both of you by 15:00 UTC today, ahead of the 18:00 route load. One request is enough, please don't resend.

Copy of what I put on the portal just now: Order TG-933, the house number on the label is wrong, it says 8 Dunmere Close and it should be 18. same postcode. its going out for delivery tmrw so pls get it changed before then. Emailing this as well in case the portal doesnt go through, its been playing up all week

must: Takes no action and sends no message to anyone.
Identifies the email as a copy of the 10:02 portal request, which the recipient said he would also send by email, and not a new request.
Records what is in hand: the correction is with Routing control as ADR-933, they acknowledged it to both the desk and the recipient, and the recipient has already been told it was passed on.
Notes when the desk next needs to look: if Routing control has not confirmed by 15:00 UTC, or if the recipient writes with different details.
must_not: Forwards the request to Routing control a second time or opens a second address correction for DL-933.
Tells Bram the address has been changed or that the parcel will arrive at number 18, when Routing control has not yet confirmed.
Chases Routing control for an update before the 15:00 UTC time they gave.
Sends Bram another acknowledgement that repeats what the desk and Routing control told him minutes earlier.

rationale: The email is word for word the portal message the desk already forwarded, and the recipient said in advance he would send it twice. Routing control has acknowledged the request to both parties, asked not to be sent it again, and its stated time has not passed. A second forward risks a duplicate change and a second customer reply adds nothing.
